slides.title: A Large Language Model-Driven Agent-Based Modeling Framework with Multi-Round Communication for Simulating Vaccine Opinion Dynamics
slides.tldr: LLM-DRIVEN AGENT-BASED MODELING FOR OPINION DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This framework integrates an LLM into agent-based modeling to simulate cognitive processes and opinion dynamics, supporting MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: An LLM-driven agent framework simulating vaccine opinion dynamics through multi-round communication and cognitive modules.
card.key_idea: Integrates Qwen3-8B into an agent-based model using memory, reflection, and diverse prompt modules to simulate how micro-level dialogues drive macro-level opinion polarization and vaccination rates.
card.evaluation: Simulated 95 agents across four scenarios using synthetic population data. Results showed non-linear social influence patterns and varying vaccination rates across cognitive configurations.
card.limitation: Small simulation scale (95 agents) due to high LLM computational costs and the absence of opinion leaders.

slides.title: Designing Touch for Trauma-Informed Social Robots: A Design Space for Direct and Indirect Actuation
slides.tldr: TRAUMA-INFORMED TOUCH DESIGN FOR SOCIAL ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This research proposes a design space for direct and indirect touch actuation in social robots to align with trauma-informed care, supporting the RwB focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A conceptual design space for creating trauma-informed touch interactions in social robots for PTSD support.
card.key_idea: Distinguishes direct and indirect touch across three dimensions: actuation modality, objective (whole/external/internal body), and intended effect (informational, functional, or affective), aligned with trauma-informed care principles.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper provides a conceptual framework and analysis rather than empirical testing or datasets.
card.limitation: The design space is exploratory and has not been empirically evaluated with PTSD patients, therapists, or other stakeholders.

slides.title: UBTech Unveils Lifelike Humanoid Robots for Emotional Companionship
slides.highlight: UBTech has introduced lifelike humanoid robots designed for emotional companionship, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: China Unveils Ultra-Realistic Humanoid Robots for Companionship
slides.highlight: The development of ultra-realistic humanoid robots for companionship is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: LLM-powered reasoning in agent-based modeling
slides.highlight: The HALE framework leverages LLMs to predict human decision-making within agent-based simulations, supporting the MIMIC goal of societal-scale simulation using LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: HALE integrates LLM reasoning into agent-based modeling to dynamically predict human mobility changes during epidemics.
card.key_idea: A hybrid framework where LLMs act as a feedback loop, updating ABM network structures by predicting group-level behavioral responses to evolving disease incidence based on demographics.
card.evaluation: Simulated COVID-19 in Salt Lake County using Llama 3.1 and synthetic populations; HALE better captured epidemic peaks than ABM-only baselines.
card.limitation: LLM inference is sensitive to prompts and temperature; it may lack sufficient information for very small municipalities.

slides.title: Multimodal Voice Activity Projection for Turn-Taking in Social Robots with Voice-Activity-Related Pretrained Encoders
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Multimodal Voice Activity Projection framework using audio-visual inputs and inter-speaker attention to anticipate conversational dynamics. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling for human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: A multimodal framework for social robots to predict turn-taking by projecting future voice activity.
card.key_idea: Combines VA-related pretrained audio-visual backbones (TalkNet, WhisperFlamingo) with LoRA adaptation, inter-speaker attention, and a semantic consistency loss to project future voice activity states.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on NoXi, NoXi+J, and Haru EDR corpora using Accuracy and F1-score; outperformed baselines, especially in shift prediction.
card.limitation: The approach was not validated under real-time conditions due to high computational resource requirements of large pretrained encoders.

slides.title: Responsible Personalisation: The Double-Edged Sword of Personalisation in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This work proposes a lifecycle-based framework to analyze ethical risks in personalised human-robot interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A framework for analyzing ethical risks of robot personalisation through an embodiment-aware, lifecycle-based lens.
card.key_idea: Combines a six-phase personalisation lifecycle with interaction contexts (duration and domain) to systematically map ethical risks like autonomy erosion and biased modelling in embodied HRI.
card.evaluation: Developed via interdisciplinary expert workshops and a review of state-of-the-art literature; no quantitative experimental results provided.
card.limitation: The framework is a conceptual tool for analysis and design rather than a tested empirical model.

slides.title: From Blueprint to Reality: Modeling and Applying Putnam's Social Capital Theory with LLM-based Multi-agent Simulations
slides.tldr: LLM-BASED SIMULATION OF SOCIAL CAPITAL THEORY
slides.highlight: SocaSim uses LLM-based multi-agent simulations to model social network evolution and trust dynamics, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: SocaSim uses LLM agents to simulate Putnam's Social Capital Theory, bridging social science and computer science.
card.key_idea: A multi-agent framework integrating Social Structure Traits, BDI decision-making, and Social Cognitive Memory to model the dynamic coupling of social networks, trust, and reciprocity norms.
card.evaluation: Validated via macro-pattern replication, counterfactual interventions, and human-agent alignment (Pearson r = 0.974) using 20 real older adults and CGSS data.
card.limitation: Relies solely on text-based interactions, lacks multimodal signals, and uses a small human sample size for alignment validation.

slides.title: Collective Cognition in Hybrid Groups: A Network Science Synthesis
slides.tldr: NETWORK SCIENCE OF HYBRID HUMAN-AI GROUPS
slides.highlight: This work synthesizes network science and collective cognition to analyze how group-level dynamics and agent-level processes shape outcomes in hybrid human-AI teams, supporting HyECHO's focus on social perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: A synthesis of network science and cognitive modeling to understand collective intelligence in human-AI hybrid groups.
card.key_idea: Integrates a Memory-Attention-Reasoning (MAR) framework with network science to analyze how node/edge heterogeneity and structural trade-offs shape hybrid collective cognition.
card.evaluation: Comparative synthesis of existing literature across human-only and AI-only networks; no new empirical experiments are conducted.
card.limitation: The framework is currently a theoretical synthesis; many hybrid-specific conjectures remain to be empirically tested.

slides.title: Institutional Red-Teaming: Deployment Rules, Not Just Models, Causally Shape Multi-Agent AI Safety
slides.tldr: EVALUATING HOW DEPLOYMENT RULES IMPACT MULTI-AGENT AI SAFETY
slides.highlight: This work introduces institutional red-teaming to analyze how deployment rules causally shape collective behavior in multi-agent systems, providing insights for the societal-scale simulation and impact analysis goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Deployment rules, not just model weights, causally determine safety outcomes in multi-agent AI systems.
card.key_idea: Institutional red-teaming isolates rule effects by holding agents and tasks fixed while varying deployment rules, specifically testing consequence allocation via the IABench-CA benchmark.
card.evaluation: Tested 7 model populations across 33,924 games (228 contexts × 5 rules). Results show rule changes shift fatality by 22–58 percentage points.
card.limitation: Uses a simplified threshold game with three agents and no communication; results may vary in complex, real-world orchestration environments.

slides.title: HumAIN: Human-Aware Implicit Social Robot Navigation
slides.highlight: The HumAIN framework uses knowledge distillation to enable real-time, socially compliant robot navigation by fusing implicit skeletal cues into the planning loop. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: HumAIN enables socially compliant robot navigation by distilling privileged human skeletal cues into a vision-only model.
card.key_idea: A transformer-based teacher model learns social representations from multi-modal data (RGB, skeletal keypoints, robot state), which are then distilled into a lightweight, real-time student model.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on SCAND and an OOD dataset against ViNT, NoMaD, GNM, and HST+MPC; improved trajectory metrics by an average of 29.8%.
card.limitation: Not yet robust for unconstrained real-world environments, particularly crowded scenes, occlusions, and diverse, unexpected human behaviors.

slides.title: A New Human-Likeness and Comfort Index for Robot Movements Along Prescribed Paths
slides.tldr: NEW INDEX FOR HUMAN-LIKE ROBOT MOVEMENT COMFORT
slides.highlight: This research introduces a human-likeness index based on the lognormality principle to predict perceived comfort in robot movements, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A new quantitative human-likeness index for robot trajectories to predict perceived human comfort a priori.
card.key_idea: The index (HL) combines the Signal-to-Noise Ratio of a sigma-lognormal velocity reconstruction with a penalty for the number of strokes used, decoupling time laws from geometric paths.
card.evaluation: Validated with 68 subjects across three experimental campaigns; results showed a consistent trend between the HL index and perceived comfort during physical robot interaction.
card.limitation: The index provides a sufficient but not necessary condition, potentially missing human-like movements influenced by spinal cord proprioceptive adjustments.

slides.title: DuplexChat: Constructing Speaker-Separated Full-Duplex Dialogue Speech at Scale for Spoken Dialogue Language Modeling
slides.highlight: This work introduces DuplexChat and a pipeline to create speaker-separated dialogue speech, contributing to HyECHO's focus on diarization and the modeling of human turn-taking dynamics.

card.one_liner: DuplexChat provides a scalable pipeline and large corpus of speaker-separated full-duplex dialogue speech.
card.key_idea: DuplexChat-Pipe crawls podcast feeds, filters for two-speaker dialogues via diarization, and uses DialogueSidon for speech separation and restoration into speaker-specific channels.
card.evaluation: Compared to Fisher corpus using DNSMOS, STOI, PESQ, ITC, and ITD; results show competitive acoustic quality and realistic turn-taking dynamics.
card.limitation: Japanese speaker separation quality is lower than English, likely due to limited training data for the DialogueSidon model.

slides.title: Embodied Human-Robot Interaction via Acoustics: A MARL Approach with AcoustoBots for Spatial Data Physicalization
slides.highlight: This work introduces AcoustoBots, which use ultrasonic phased arrays to levitate particles as communication cues, contributing to the study of embodied human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: AcoustoBots use mobile robots and acoustic levitation to physically render spatial data as particle heights.
card.key_idea: Combines TurtleBot3s with ultrasonic phased arrays and MADDPG-based MARL to navigate and encode urban scalar values (1–10 cm height) via a GS-PAT acoustic controller.
card.evaluation: Tested on a 4m x 3m scaled UK map; achieved 90% success for single-robot traversal and 80% for dual-robot coverage over 10 trials each.
card.limitation: Evaluated with a small number of robots in a simplified 2D grid-world abstraction, potentially limiting real-world scalability.

slides.title: Diarization-Guided Qwen-ASR Adaptation for Multilingual Two-Speaker Conversational Speech
slides.highlight: This work presents a system combining speaker diarization with an adapted ASR model for two-speaker conversational speech, contributing to HyECHO's focus on diarization and social perception in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: A diarization-guided Qwen-ASR system for multilingual two-speaker conversations using synthetic data and GRPO reinforcement learning.
card.key_idea: Combines a modular diarization front end with Qwen3-ASR-1.7B, adapted via supervised fine-tuning, TTS-based synthetic LoRA augmentation, and GRPO reinforcement learning to penalize hallucinations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on MLC-SLM 2026 official sets; achieved 17.97 average tcpMER on the final set, improving upon the baseline Qwen-ASR-1.7B.

slides.title: SPEARBench: A Benchmark for Naturalness Evaluation in Streaming Speech-to-Speech Language Models
slides.highlight: SPEARBench evaluates naturalness in speech-to-speech models, focusing on timing, turn-taking, and interpersonal stance, which aligns with HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: SPEARBench is an automated benchmark for evaluating conversational naturalness in streaming speech-to-speech language models.
card.key_idea: It uses controlled dialogue prompts from the Seamless Interaction corpus to evaluate models across latency, interruptions, prosody, emotional naturalness, dialect consistency, and interpersonal stance.
card.evaluation: Evaluated seven S2S models (e.g., GPT-realtime-2, Gemini-3.1) using ASR, UTMOS, and specialized predictors; results show models lack human-like emotional entrainment and pitch variation.
card.limitation: Evaluation is fully automatic, limited to English-only two-speaker dialogues, and timing measures depend on model serving interfaces.

slides.title: Meta launches flagship Muse Spark 1.1 model with multi-agent upgrades
slides.highlight: The introduction of multi-agent upgrades in the Muse Spark 1.1 model is relevant to MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

slides.title: Prompt Coach: An Empirical Evaluation of an Agentic Tutor for Learning Prompt Engineering in Software Development
slides.highlight: This work introduces an agentic tutor that uses Socratic guidance and targeted questions to help users self-correct, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and meta-cognition.

card.one_liner: Prompt Coach is an agentic IDE tutor that teaches developers prompt engineering via Socratic guidance.
card.key_idea: A multi-agent system that evaluates prompts across eight dimensions and uses codebase context and LLM behavior to provide reflective, non-prescriptive questions for self-correction.
card.evaluation: Tested with 15 professional developers using APPS benchmark tasks; showed 13.73% improvement in prompt quality and high user trust/adoption readiness.
card.limitation: Small sample size from one organization, limited 60-minute sessions, and evaluation conducted without real-world project context.

slides.title: Meta Superintelligence Labs Releases Muse Spark 1.1
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL REASONING MODEL FOR AGENTIC TASKS
slides.highlight: Muse Spark 1.1 provides multimodal reasoning for agentic tasks, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and hybrid human-AI team states.

slides.title: Context-Aware Force Estimation for Deformable Tool Manipulation in Robotic Environmental Swabbing via Few-Shot Continual Adaptation
slides.tldr: FORCE ESTIMATION FOR DEFORMABLE TOOL MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work presents a data-driven framework for estimating contact forces in deformable tool manipulation using a recurrent architecture and few-shot adaptation. It is relevant to MOSAIC's focus on physics and force-based human proficiency estimation and adaptive AI coaching.

card.one_liner: A context-aware LSTM framework for estimating tip-level contact forces in robotic swabbing using proprioceptive sensing.
card.key_idea: A frozen LSTM backbone captures deformation history, while low-dimensional context embeddings via FiLM enable few-shot adaptation to new surfaces and tool compliance without catastrophic forgetting.
card.evaluation: Tested on a UR5e across nine tool-surface regimes; LSTM outperformed Transformers/TCNs, reducing zero-shot estimation error by up to 63% after few-shot adaptation.

slides.title: The User-In-Context Framework: Understanding Variation in How Users Respond to AI Chatbots
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework for understanding the reciprocal and coadaptive interactions between users and personalized AI, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on human-AI coadaptation.

card.one_liner: A heuristic framework based on Bronfenbrenner's theory to explain variable human responses to personalized AI chatbots.
card.key_idea: Adapts ecological systems theory to model reciprocal, coadaptive interactions between users and stateful AICs, accounting for contextual factors and user-influenced AI memory.
card.limitation: The paper presents a heuristic framework rather than an empirically tested model with quantitative results.

slides.title: BUS: Brain-Inspired Unsupervised Self-Reflection for Advanced Multimodal Reasoning
slides.highlight: This work introduces a label-free framework for self-reflective reasoning based on backward prediction, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and self-correction via meta-cognition.

card.one_liner: BUS improves VLM multimodal reasoning using a brain-inspired, label-free self-reflection framework based on backward prediction.
card.key_idea: BUS trains VLMs to perform backward prediction—predicting which reasoning paths likely precede a given answer—enabling self-verification and reflective reasoning without ground-truth labels.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 8 benchmarks (including MME-RealWorld-Lite, HR-Bench, and MathVista) using Qwen3-VL; results show significant improvements over base models and other self-reflection methods.
